decision: vitest 3 as the runner, tests drive the real Hono app in-process with app.request and assert through SQL
why: no new server, no mocks; the same paths the desk and the parent's browser hit

decision: split apps/api/src/index.ts into app.ts (routes, exported appWithRoutes) and index.ts (serve + scheduler)
why: importing the entry started a server and the scheduler; tests need the app without either

decision: one test database per run, dropped and recreated in globalSetup, migrated with the project's own pnpm db:migrate via execFileSync
why: the schema under test must be what production gets; no drizzle-orm import outside @repo/db; no shell string
result: 26 migrations applied, harness asserts the count

decision: FINDING RH-01: the API carried better-auth's nextCookies() plugin (a Next.js-only integration); every server-side auth.api.* call tried to import next/headers, which does not exist in the API process
why: under plain Node the import failure was swallowed so desk onboarding only appeared to work; under vitest it surfaced and every desk onboarding returned 'Failed to onboard family'
evidence: apps/api/src/lib/auth.ts (plugin removed with a comment); error text 'Cannot find module .../next/headers' in the test log at 20:14
result: removed; suite reached the money paths

decision: clientMessage now logs whatever it hides from the client
why: with RF-07 the client gets a generic sentence, so the operator log must carry the real cause or nothing does; this is how RH-01 was found

decision: test isolation: the V3 suite deletes its school-fee schedule when done (plus an afterAll safety net); takings are asserted as deltas from a snapshot; files run in name order via a sequencer
why: the suites share one database and one calendar day; first full run showed the fee schedule gating the desk suite and takings summing across files

decision: tests rewritten onto the Hono RPC client (hc<AppType> bound to app.request); raw requests remain only for the two better-auth endpoints outside the typed surface
why: the user's rule: every request to the backend goes through the RPC client for end-to-end types; the apps use better-auth's own client for sign-in, so tests do the same

decision: FINDING RH-02 (root cause of the repo's 'RPC infers never' quirk): success() typed its body through c.json<ApiResponse<T>>, and Hono's JSONParsed mapped type dropped the data key while T was a deferred generic, so every route using success() typed as { success: true } on the client and apiResponse inferred never
why: the memory file and the web code both carried this as a known quirk worked around with explicit casts; the cause was one helper
evidence: apps/api/src/lib/response.ts SuccessResponse/ErrorResponse with JSONParsed applied to data only; probe at 20:41 showed '{ success: true; message?: string }' with no data

decision: consequence of RH-02: the web app's workaround casts and explicit useQuery generics now conflict with the real types (44 errors in a handful of screens); cleaning them up is the next step, not reverting the fix
why: reverting would keep every RPC call site untyped, the opposite of the project's stated goal
evidence: apps/web check-types after the helper fix

decision: three tests added at the fix reviewer's request: desk refuses money for a student with no linked parent but still registers; desk-pay refuses a waived fee; a second schedule for the same year answers 409
why: each covers a gap the reviewer found in the spine fixes

decision: observation for the notification audit: the InstaPay confirmation says 'Payment of EGP 1500.00 via instapay' when 1000 was transferred and 500 came from escrow
why: the family reads the settled total, not what left their bank

decision: web cleanup after RH-02: removed the eight manual useQuery generics that now conflicted, derived four screens' row types from their RPC fetchers (Awaited<ReturnType<typeof fetchX>>[number]) instead of hand-written interfaces, narrowed the escrow balance union
why: PATTERNS.md golden rule one: never manually type API responses; the hand-written types had drifted from the API (an escrow variant without heldBalance, a change-request shape that differed by role)
evidence: apps/web approvals, pending-requests, escrow, history, checkout client files; web check-types 44 -> 0

decision: API change: the student's own change-request listing now includes registration.student like the parent listing, so GET /v1/change-requests has one response type
why: the route serves two roles from two service functions; a union that differs by role forces every screen to narrow

decision: left 38 manual useQuery generics elsewhere in the web app that happen to agree with the real types
why: they compile today but each one can drift; removing them is a mechanical follow-up for the engineering-health audit

decision: checkpoint: all gates green before commit
why: done means proven
